stem.en: Why are there generally far fewer safe, effective antifungal and antiparasitic drugs available compared to antibacterial drugs?
stem.et: Miks on üldiselt saadaval palju vähem ohutuid, tõhusaid seene- ja parasiidivastaseid ravimeid võrreldes antibakteriaalsete ravimitega?

label.en: Because fungi and parasites are eukaryotic and share much more cellular machinery with human cells than bacteria do, making it much harder to find a drug target present in the pathogen but safely absent from human cells.
label.et: Sest seened ja parasiidid on eukarüootsed ning jagavad palju rohkem raku masinavärki inimrakkudega kui bakterid, mistõttu on palju raskem leida ravimisihtmärki, mis on patogeenis olemas, kuid inimrakkudest ohutult puudub.

label.en: Because fungi and parasites are simply more complex, larger versions of bacteria, so existing antibiotics already work reasonably well against them and little further drug development has been needed.
label.et: Sest seened ja parasiidid on lihtsalt keerukamad, suuremad bakterite versioonid, mistõttu olemasolevad antibiootikumid juba toimivad nende vastu mõistlikult hästi ja täiendavat ravimiarendust pole vaja olnud.

label.en: There actually isn't a meaningful difference in the number of available drug classes -- antifungal and antiparasitic drugs are just as numerous and just as selective as antibacterial drugs.
label.et: Tegelikult ei ole saadaolevate ravimiklasside arvus olulist erinevust -- seene- ja parasiidivastased ravimid on sama arvukad ja sama selektiivsed kui antibakteriaalsed ravimid.

label.en: Because fungal and parasitic infections are so immediately obvious and severe that they are usually treated with surgery rather than drugs, reducing the need for pharmaceutical development.
label.et: Sest seen- ja parasiitinfektsioonid on nii kohe ilmsed ja tõsised, et neid ravitakse tavaliselt kirurgiliselt, mitte ravimitega, vähendades farmaatsiaarenduse vajadust.
